title: A Journey through States of Water

learn.hook: Water is a shape-shifter! It can be a hard ice cube, a splashing liquid or an invisible gas in the air.
points: Water can exist in three states: solid (ice), liquid (water) and gas (water vapour).
A solid has a fixed shape and a fixed volume. An ice cube keeps its shape in any glass.
A liquid has a fixed volume but no fixed shape; it takes the shape of its container.
A gas has neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume; it spreads out to fill all the space it gets. Water vapour is invisible.
All matter is made of tiny particles. In solids they are packed very close, in liquids a little apart, and in gases far apart and moving freely.

example.q: Rohit pours 200 mL of water from a tall glass into a flat bowl. What changes and what stays the same?
steps: Water is a liquid.
Liquids take the shape of their container, so the shape changes from tall to flat.
Liquids have a fixed volume, so the amount stays 200 mL.
example.answer: The shape changes, but the volume stays 200 mL.

learn.reallife: In your kitchen you can see all three states of water: ice cubes from the freezer, water in a jug, and invisible water vapour rising from a boiling pot (the white mist you see is tiny droplets that formed as the vapour cooled).

quiz.q: What are the three states of water?
quiz.explain: Water exists as solid (ice), liquid (water) and gas (water vapour).
steps: Water exists in three states: solid, liquid and gas.
Solid = ice, liquid = water, gas = water vapour.
So the three states are ice, water and water vapour.
Answer: Ice, water and water vapour
quiz.mistake: Lists different forms of the same state

quiz.q: Which state has a fixed shape and a fixed volume?
quiz.explain: A solid, like an ice cube, keeps its shape and volume.
steps: A solid has a fixed shape and a fixed volume.
An ice cube keeps its shape in any glass.
Liquids and gases do not have a fixed shape.
So the answer is solid.
Answer: Solid
quiz.mistake: Confuses solids with liquids

quiz.q: Which state takes the shape of its container but has a fixed volume?
quiz.explain: Liquids flow and take the container's shape, but their volume does not change.
steps: A liquid has a fixed volume but no fixed shape.
It takes the shape of its container.
So the answer is liquid.
Answer: Liquid
quiz.mistake: Mixes up liquids and gases

quiz.q: Why can't we see water vapour in the air?
options: It is a gas and is invisible
It is always hidden in clouds
quiz.explain: Water vapour is an invisible gas. Clouds and mist are tiny liquid droplets.
steps: Water vapour is water in the gas state.
Water vapour is invisible.
Clouds and mist are tiny liquid droplets, not vapour.
So we cannot see it because it is an invisible gas.
Answer: It is a gas and is invisible
quiz.mistake: Thinks clouds or steam are water vapour

quiz.q: In which state are the particles farthest apart?
options: They are equally far in all states
quiz.explain: Gas particles are far apart and move freely, which is why gases spread out.
steps: Solids: particles packed very close; liquids: a little apart.
Gases: particles far apart and moving freely.
So particles are farthest apart in a gas.
Answer: Gas
quiz.mistake: Thinks particles are the same distance apart in all states

quiz.q: A gas spreads out to fill:
options: All the space available to it
Only the bottom of a container
quiz.explain: Gases have no fixed volume, so they fill any space they get.
steps: A gas has no fixed shape or volume.
It spreads out to fill all the space it gets.
So it fills all the space available to it.
Answer: All the space available to it
quiz.mistake: Thinks gases have a fixed volume

quiz.q: Which of these is water in the solid state?
quiz.explain: A hailstone is a ball of ice, which is solid water.
steps: Solid water is ice.
A hailstone is a ball of ice.
Dew and rain are liquid; water vapour is gas.
So the hailstone is solid water.
Answer: Hailstone
quiz.mistake: Confuses solid and liquid forms of water

quiz.q: Meera pours 1 litre of milk from a jug into a round pot. What is the volume in the pot?
options: It depends on the pot's shape
quiz.explain: A liquid keeps its volume when poured, so it is still 1 litre.
steps: A liquid has a fixed volume.
Pouring changes its shape, not its volume.
So the pot holds 1 litre.
Answer: 1 litre
quiz.mistake: Thinks the volume of a liquid changes with the container

teach.ask: Gappu looks at an ice cube, a glass of water and a steaming kettle: 'Are these all water? Why do they look so different?'
teach.praise: Wow! Ice is solid, water is liquid and water vapour is gas. Same water, three states!
teach.nudge: What are the three states? And how is the shape of a solid different from a liquid's?

revise.summary: Water exists as solid (ice), liquid (water) and gas (water vapour). Solids have fixed shape and volume, liquids have fixed volume only, and gases have neither.
focus: Properties of solids, liquids and gases (shape and volume)
Arrangement of particles in each state
Examples of water in each state
remember: Liquid: fixed volume, takes the container's shape (water)
Gas: no fixed shape or volume, fills all space; water vapour is invisible
Particles: very close in solids, a little apart in liquids, far apart in gases
traps: Pouring a liquid changes its shape, not its volume.
Clouds and mist are not water vapour; they are tiny liquid droplets.

learn.hook: Where does the water from wet clothes go? And where do the drops on a cold glass come from? Same water, opposite journeys!
points: Evaporation: liquid water slowly changes into water vapour from its surface. It happens at all temperatures, not only when water boils.
Evaporation is faster when it is hotter, when there is wind, when the water is spread over a larger area, and when the air is less humid (less moist).
Evaporation causes cooling: sweat cools our body, and water in an earthen matka or surahi stays cool as water seeping through it evaporates.
Condensation: water vapour cools and changes back into liquid water, like droplets on the outside of a cold glass, dew on grass, and a foggy bathroom mirror.
Water cycle: water evaporates from seas, rivers and land, condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds, and falls back as rain, snow or hail.

example.q: Pooja hangs one wet dupatta spread out and another folded, both in the sun. Which dries first, and why?
steps: Both are in the sun, so the temperature is the same.
The spread-out dupatta has a larger surface exposed to air.
A larger surface area makes evaporation faster.
example.answer: The spread-out dupatta dries first because more of its surface is open to the air.

learn.reallife: On winter mornings in North India you can see dew drops on grass and leaves. In summer, a matka keeps drinking water cool without a fridge.

quiz.q: What is evaporation?
options: Liquid water changing into water vapour
quiz.explain: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface.
steps: Evaporation is a change of state from the surface of a liquid.
Liquid water slowly changes into water vapour.
Vapour to liquid is condensation; water to ice is freezing.
So evaporation is liquid water changing into water vapour.
Answer: Liquid water changing into water vapour
quiz.mistake: Confuses evaporation with condensation or freezing

quiz.q: Why do drops of water appear on the outside of a glass of iced water?
options: The ice melts through the glass
Water vapour in the air condenses on the cold glass
The glass is sweating like a person
quiz.explain: The cold glass cools the water vapour in the surrounding air, and it changes into droplets.
steps: The air around the glass has water vapour.
The cold glass cools this vapour.
Cooled vapour condenses into liquid droplets.
So water vapour in the air condenses on the cold glass.
Answer: Water vapour in the air condenses on the cold glass
quiz.mistake: Thinks the water leaks out from inside the glass

quiz.q: On which day will wet clothes dry the fastest?
options: A cold, still and humid day
A hot, sunny and windy day
quiz.explain: Heat, wind and dry air all make evaporation faster.
steps: Evaporation is faster when it is hotter, windy and the air is less humid.
A hot, sunny and windy day has all of these.
Cold, still, humid, rainy or foggy days slow drying.
So clothes dry fastest on a hot, sunny and windy day.
Answer: A hot, sunny and windy day
quiz.mistake: Does not know the factors that affect evaporation

quiz.q: Why does water in an earthen matka stay cool?
options: Clay makes water cold by magic
The matka is kept in the sun
Water seeping out through tiny pores evaporates and cools the pot
quiz.explain: Evaporation takes heat from the pot and the water, cooling them.
steps: Water seeps out through tiny pores in the matka.
It evaporates from the surface.
Evaporation causes cooling.
So the water stays cool because seeping water evaporates and cools the pot.
Answer: Water seeping out through tiny pores evaporates and cools the pot
quiz.mistake: Does not know that evaporation causes cooling

quiz.q: Dew drops on grass on a winter morning are formed by:
quiz.explain: Water vapour in the air cools at night and condenses on the cool grass.
steps: At night, water vapour in the air cools.
It changes back into liquid on the cool grass.
Vapour to liquid is condensation.
So dew forms by condensation.
Answer: Condensation
quiz.mistake: Mixes up condensation and evaporation

quiz.q: Does evaporation happen only when water boils?
options: No, it happens at all temperatures
No, it happens only in winter
quiz.explain: A puddle dries on a normal day without boiling. Evaporation goes on at all temperatures.
steps: Evaporation happens at all temperatures, not only when water boils.
A puddle dries on a normal day without boiling.
So No, it happens at all temperatures.
Answer: No, it happens at all temperatures
quiz.mistake: Thinks evaporation and boiling are the same

quiz.q: How are clouds formed?
options: Smoke from chimneys collects in the sky
Ice is thrown up from the sea
Water vapour cools and condenses into tiny droplets
quiz.explain: Rising water vapour cools high up and condenses into tiny droplets that make clouds.
steps: Water evaporates from seas, rivers and land.
Rising water vapour cools and condenses into tiny droplets.
These droplets form clouds.
So clouds form when water vapour cools and condenses into tiny droplets.
Answer: Water vapour cools and condenses into tiny droplets
quiz.mistake: Does not link clouds with condensation

quiz.q: Why do we feel cool when sweat dries on our skin?
options: Evaporation of sweat takes away heat from the body
quiz.explain: As sweat evaporates, it takes heat from our body, so we feel cooler.
steps: Evaporation causes cooling.
As sweat evaporates, it takes away heat from the body.
So we feel cool.
Answer: Evaporation of sweat takes away heat from the body
quiz.mistake: Does not know that evaporation causes cooling

teach.ask: Gappu stares at his empty water dish: 'I left water here this morning. Now it's gone! And why is my cold glass wet outside?'
teach.praise: Tweet! The water in my dish evaporated into vapour, and vapour in the air condensed on the cold glass. Opposite journeys!
teach.nudge: Where did the water in the dish go? And what turns the vapour back into drops?

revise.summary: Evaporation changes liquid water into vapour from its surface at any temperature and causes cooling. Condensation changes vapour back to liquid. Together they drive the water cycle.
focus: Cooling by evaporation: sweat, matka, surahi
Examples of condensation: cold glass, dew, foggy mirror
How clouds and rain form in the water cycle
remember: Evaporation: liquid → vapour, from the surface, at all temperatures
Faster when hotter, windy, spread out and less humid
traps: Don't think evaporation happens only when water boils.
Drops on a cold glass do not leak through; they come from vapour in the air.
Dew forms by condensation, not evaporation.

learn.hook: Leave a kulfi out in May and see how fast it turns into a puddle! That's melting in action.
points: Melting: a solid changes into a liquid on heating. Ice melts at 0 °C.
Freezing: a liquid changes into a solid on cooling. Pure water freezes at 0 °C.
So melting and freezing are opposite changes, and for water both happen at 0 °C.
Boiling: water changes quickly into vapour at 100 °C, with bubbles forming throughout the liquid.
Water expands when it freezes, so ice is lighter than the same volume of water and floats. A glass bottle filled to the top with water can crack in a freezer.

example.q: Ice cubes are put into a glass of water. Do they sink or float, and why?
steps: When water freezes, it expands and takes up more space.
So a piece of ice is lighter than the same volume of water.
Things lighter than the same volume of water float.
example.answer: They float, because ice is lighter than the same volume of water.

learn.reallife: Snow on the Himalayas melts in summer and feeds rivers like the Ganga. Kulfi and ice cream are made by freezing.

games.title: Name the change

games.title: Melt or freeze?
items: Freezing is the change from solid to liquid.
Freezing is liquid to solid. Solid to liquid is melting.
Ice is lighter than the same volume of water.
Melting snow on mountains helps fill rivers.
Snow-fed rivers like the Ganga get water from melting snow and ice.
Pure water boils at 100 °C at normal air pressure.
That is the boiling point of water on the Celsius scale.

quiz.q: What is melting?
options: A liquid changing into a solid
A solid changing into a liquid
A liquid changing into a gas
A gas changing into a liquid
quiz.explain: When ice is heated, it melts into water: solid to liquid.
steps: Melting: a solid changes into a liquid on heating.
Example: ice melts into water.
So melting is a solid changing into a liquid.
Answer: A solid changing into a liquid
quiz.mistake: Mixes up melting with freezing

quiz.q: At what temperature does pure water freeze, in °C?
quiz.explain: Pure water freezes at 0 °C, the same temperature at which ice melts.
steps: Freezing: liquid to solid on cooling.
Pure water freezes at 0 °C, the same temperature at which ice melts.
So the answer is 0.
Answer: 0
quiz.mistake: Confuses freezing point with boiling point

quiz.q: Water kept in the freezer turns into ice. This is:
quiz.explain: A liquid changing into a solid on cooling is freezing.
steps: In the freezer, liquid water cools and becomes solid ice.
Liquid to solid on cooling is freezing.
So it is freezing.
Answer: Freezing
quiz.mistake: Mixes up freezing and melting

quiz.q: Why does ice float on water?
options: Ice has air bubbles only on top
Ice is lighter than the same volume of water
quiz.explain: Water expands on freezing, so ice is lighter than the same volume of water and floats.
steps: Water expands when it freezes.
So ice is lighter than the same volume of water.
Lighter things float on water.
So ice floats because it is lighter than the same volume of water.
Answer: Ice is lighter than the same volume of water
quiz.mistake: Thinks solids are always heavier than their liquids

quiz.q: Why can a glass bottle filled to the top with water crack in the freezer?
quiz.explain: As water turns to ice it takes up more space and pushes on the bottle.
steps: Water expands when it freezes.
The ice needs more space than the water did.
It pushes on the full bottle and can crack it.
So the reason is: water expands when it freezes.
Answer: Water expands when it freezes
quiz.mistake: Thinks water shrinks when it freezes

quiz.q: Melting and freezing are:
quiz.explain: Melting is solid to liquid; freezing is liquid to solid. They are opposites.
steps: Melting: solid → liquid. Freezing: liquid → solid.
One is the reverse of the other.
So they are opposite changes.
Answer: Opposite changes
quiz.mistake: Does not see the reverse relationship

quiz.q: A kulfi left on a plate on a hot day turns into a liquid. What has happened?
quiz.explain: Heat from the surroundings turns the solid kulfi into liquid: melting.
steps: The kulfi is a solid.
Heat from the hot day turns it into a liquid.
Solid to liquid is melting.
So it has melted.
Answer: It has melted
quiz.mistake: Confuses melting with other changes

quiz.q: How does boiling differ from evaporation?
options: Boiling happens quickly at a fixed temperature with bubbles throughout; evaporation happens slowly from the surface at any temperature
quiz.explain: Water boils at 100 °C with bubbles inside the liquid, while evaporation goes on quietly from the surface at any temperature.
steps: Boiling: quick change to vapour at 100 °C with bubbles throughout the liquid.
Evaporation: slow change from the surface at any temperature.
So boiling is quick at a fixed temperature with bubbles; evaporation is slow from the surface at any temperature.
Answer: Boiling happens quickly at a fixed temperature with bubbles throughout; evaporation happens slowly from the surface at any temperature
quiz.mistake: Thinks boiling and evaporation are the same process

teach.ask: Gappu watches an ice cube in the sun: 'It's turning into water! And my water in the freezer became ice. What are these changes called?'
teach.praise: Hooray! Heating ice makes it melt, cooling water makes it freeze, and both happen at 0 °C for water!
teach.nudge: What do we call ice turning into water? And what about water turning into ice? At what temperature?

revise.summary: Melting turns a solid into a liquid and freezing turns a liquid into a solid; for water both happen at 0 °C. Water boils at 100 °C, and water expands on freezing, so ice floats.
focus: Melting and freezing as opposite changes
Why ice floats and bottles crack in the freezer
remember: Melting: solid → liquid; freezing: liquid → solid; both at 0 °C for water
Water expands on freezing, so ice is lighter than the same volume of water
traps: Don't say water shrinks when it freezes; it expands.
Boiling and evaporation are not the same: evaporation is slow and only at the surface.
